items.title: Maxwell stress divergence for classical fields

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, sections II.1–II.2
references.locator: Context for Maxwell stress and its observer split. The finite-regularity identity with the local SI normalization is proved directly here.

items.design_state: Local classical Maxwell stress prerequisite authored in bounded Step2 owner repair; scientific source disposition recorded separately; metadata/readiness/native gates remain.
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented four-manifold, let
$g$ be a time-oriented $C^1$ Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and
let $F$ be a real $C^1$ two-form with $dF=0$. Use the connection and stress
conventions of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], interpreted here by
their explicit coordinate formulas at this regularity. Fix $\mu_0>0$ and put

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}=\mu_0^{-1}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right).$$

The Christoffel formula defines a continuous metric-compatible torsion-free
connection, $T^{\mathrm{EM}}$ is $C^1$, and the following continuous
pointwise identity holds:

$$\nabla_a(T^{\mathrm{EM}})^a{}_b=\mu_0^{-1}F_{bc}\nabla_aF^{ac}.$$

In particular, if a continuous vector field $J$ satisfies
$\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$, then
$\nabla^aT^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}=-F_{bc}J^c$. For $J=0$ the stress is
conserved. No Einstein equation, smoothness of $F$ beyond $C^1$, or global
potential/exactness hypothesis is needed.

At each point, for a future unit normal $n$ and a positively oriented
orthonormal spatial basis $(\mathsf e_i)$, set
$e_i=F(\mathsf e_i,n)$ and
$b_i=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k)$, with
$\epsilon_{123}=1$. The algebraic observer identities are

$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}(n,n)=\frac{|e|^2+|b|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}(n,X)=-\frac{1}{\mu_0}\langle e\times b,X\rangle$$

for every spatial $X$. These formulas have the same signs and normalization
as the smooth electrovacuum convention. They assert no field existence or
regularity threshold for a coupled PDE.

items.title: Positive symmetric Maxwell field-strength reduction

items.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\Sigma$ be a coordinate neighborhood in an oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, foliated by spacelike $s$-levels. Write
$$g=-\alpha^2ds^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i ds)(dx^j+\beta^j ds),\qquad \alpha>0,\qquad h=(h_{ij})>0,$$
and let $n=\alpha^{-1}(\partial_s-\beta^i\partial_i)$ be the future unit normal. On a smaller neighborhood choose a positively oriented orthonormal spatial frame $(\mathsf e_1,\mathsf e_2,\mathsf e_3)$ by Gram–Schmidt. Let $D$ be the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$, define $\operatorname{div}_h v:=D_iv^i$ and $(\operatorname{curl}_h v)_i:=\epsilon_i{}^{jk}D_jv_k$, and define the spatial cross product by $(u\times v)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$ in this frame. For a smooth real two-form $F$, define the real spatial components $e_i:=F(\mathsf e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k)$, with $\epsilon_{123}=1$; thus $F_{0i}=-e_i$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$ in the adapted tetrad. Assume the source-free model of draft definition [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], whose actual equations are $dF=0$ and $d\star_gF=0$; its draft status and manifest omission are recorded in [L1].

The six evolution equations for $(e,b)$ have principal part
$$n(e)-\operatorname{curl}_h b=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b),\qquad n(b)+\operatorname{curl}_h e=\text{terms with no derivatives of }(e,b).$$
For a spatial covector $\xi$, let $C(\xi)v:=\xi^\sharp\times v$ in the oriented orthonormal frame. Set $\theta^0:=\alpha ds=-g(n,\cdot)$ and decompose any spacetime covector as $\zeta=\zeta(n)\theta^0+\zeta_\perp$, where $\zeta_\perp(n)=0$ and $|\zeta_\perp|_h$ is its spatial norm. The spatial principal block is the linear map on $\mathbb R^3\oplus\mathbb R^3$ defined by $S(\xi)(u,v)=(-C(\xi)v,C(\xi)u)$. It is real symmetric, has eigenvalues $0,0,|\xi|,|\xi|,-|\xi|,-|\xi|$, and satisfies $\|S(\xi)\|=|\xi|$. Therefore the principal symbol $P(\zeta)=\zeta(n)I_6+S(\zeta_\perp)$ is positive definite for every covector with $\zeta(n)>|\zeta_\perp|_h$. In the adapted coordinates its time matrix is $\alpha^{-1}I_6$, and every coordinate spatial matrix is symmetric. Derivatives of the frame and metric enter only as smooth lower-order coefficients depending on $(g,g^{-1},\partial g,e,b)$; in a first-order metric state they are zero-order terms. The remaining two Maxwell equations are the constraints $\operatorname{div}_h e=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_h b=0$.

items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth oriented four-manifold with a time-oriented $C^1$ Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Let a neighborhood of the initial slice $\Sigma_0$ have a $C^1$ spacelike foliation with a $C^1$ future unit normal field $n$, transverse to $\Sigma_0$. Here the normal's $C^1$ regularity is an explicit hypothesis; a merely $C^1$ defining time function alone need not provide it. Smooth coordinate time levels with a $C^1$ metric satisfy this hypothesis. Let $F$ be a $C^1$ real two-form on this neighborhood. Define its electric and magnetic spatial vectors by $e_i=F(\mathsf e_i,n)$ and $b_i=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k)$ in a positively oriented orthonormal spatial frame. Suppose the six evolution equations are
$$\iota_n dF=0,\qquad \iota_n d(\star_gF)=0,$$
and suppose the initial Gauss constraints are $D_ie^i=0$ and $D_ib^i=0$ on $\Sigma_0$, where $D$ is the Levi-Civita derivative of its induced $C^1$ Riemannian metric $h$. These six equations are the normal-slot component equations of the field-strength reduction [[lem-emg-fieldstrength-positive-symmetric-reduction]]; their displayed first-derivative formulation is used here directly, without assuming that supplier's smooth-field hypotheses. Then $dF=0$ and $d(\star_gF)=0$ on a neighborhood of each point of $\Sigma_0$. No Einstein equation, stress conservation law, smooth potential, or global exactness of $F$ is needed.

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $s\ge5$ be an integer and let $U=(g_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi},e_i,b_i)$ be the finite-dimensional first-order state on the $2\pi$-periodic three-torus, with $p_{ab}= ar
abla_0g_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}= ar
abla_i g_{ab}$ for a fixed smooth background connection $ ar
abla$. The component Sobolev spaces $H^s$ are those of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Assume an open admissible state set $O$ on which $g$ is Lorentzian, $g^{00}<0$, the inverse spatial block $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite, the lapse is positive, and the chosen state variables and coefficients are smooth. Let $K\Subset\operatorname{int}K'\Subset O$ be compact sets and $R\ge0$. Assume the draft local symmetric-hyperbolic supplier [[thm-emg-symmetric-hyperbolic-research-supplier]] with its stated integer-$s$, coefficient, compact-state, choice and norm hypotheses. Then the harmonic-coordinate reduced Einstein equation with source $T_{ab}=\mu_0^{-1}(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-	frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd})$, coupled to the six source-free Maxwell field-strength evolution equations, is a smooth quasilinear symmetric-hyperbolic system. For every initial state $U_0\in H^s$ taking values in $K$ and satisfying $\|U_0\|_{H^s}\le R$, its reduced system has a local solution with the regularity and compact-state bounds of [[thm-emg-symmetric-hyperbolic-research-supplier]]. No Einstein or Maxwell constraint is assumed in this reduced-system statement.

items.statement: Let $(g,F)$ be a reduced Einstein–Maxwell solution with $g\in C^3$ and $F\in C^2$ on a neighborhood of a smooth spacelike initial hypersurface $\Sigma_0$. Let the initial metric and first derivatives be chosen by [[lem-emg-fixed-smooth-background-harmonic-data]], so the harmonic vector $H^a:=g^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$ vanishes on $\Sigma_0$. Assume the source-free Maxwell divergence constraints and the four Einstein Hamiltonian/momentum constraints hold on $\Sigma_0$. Using the classical stress identity below and the stated normal constraint identities, $H=0$ on a neighborhood of each point of $\Sigma_0$, and the reduced metric equation there is the full Einstein–Maxwell equation.

items.title: Local high-Sobolev and smooth electrovacuum

references.title: P. T. Chruściel, An introduction to the Cauchy problem for the Einstein equations, Roscoff lecture notes (2011), §1.6, printed pp. 23–25.
M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009), §II and §II.C, printed pp. 3–9.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. Fix $L_0>0$ in metres and put $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi L_0}$ with length coordinates $X^i$. On $\Sigma$, let $h\in H^{s+1}$ be a symmetric Riemannian metric with $h\ge c_0 I$ for some $c_0>0$, let $K\in H^s$ be a symmetric covariant two-tensor, and let $e,b\in H^s$ be spatial vector fields. Sobolev membership means that the length-frame arrays $h_{ij},K_{ij}$ and oriented orthonormal arrays $e_A,b_A$, composed with $D_{L_0}:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\Sigma$, $[\theta]\mapsto[L_0\theta]$, belong to the real componentwise Fourier spaces of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]; these are not tensor pullbacks. All spatial derivatives in the geometric equations are $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$. Use the length coordinate $t=x^0=ct_{\rm SI}$, so $g,h$ are dimensionless, $K$ has units $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and $e=E/c$ and $b=B$ both have units tesla in an oriented orthonormal frame; $\kappa\mu_0^{-1}|e|^2$ has units $\mathrm m^{-2}$. Use the sign convention $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ for the future unit normal. Assume
$$D_ie^i=0,\qquad D_ib^i=0,\qquad R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2),\qquad D^jK_{ji}-D_i\operatorname{tr}_hK=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_h b)_i,$$
where $D$ is the Levi-Civita derivative of $h$. Then there are $T>0$ and a solution of the full source-free Einstein–Maxwell system on $(-T,T)\times\Sigma$ with
$$g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C^0H^s,\qquad \partial_tg\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1},\qquad F\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}.$$
The initial two-form is reconstructed by $F(n,\mathsf e_i)=-e_i$ and $F(\mathsf e_i,\mathsf e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$; no independent Maxwell normal derivative is prescribed. The metric remains Lorentzian with spacelike $t$-levels in a fixed compact admissible state neighborhood. Smooth data give a smooth solution on the same base-order interval. For a fixed harmonic background, on any common local interval with the stated compact-state and uniform $H^s$ bounds, the harmonic-reduced first-order state is unique and continuously dependent on its initial state in $C^0H^{s-1}$. In addition, on any smooth oriented three-manifold, smooth constrained data with these same equations have a smooth full development in a neighborhood of each initial point. For finite-Sobolev data these equations mean their classical pointwise form at the $C^3$ metric and $C^2$ field regularity proved below; smoothness is asserted only for smooth initial data. No endpoint regularity threshold, strong $C^0H^s$ stability, global continuation, or geodesic completeness is asserted. Here an affinely parametrized metric geodesic solves $\ddot x^a+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\dot x^b\dot x^c=0$ on an interval; a maximal such solution admits no extension to a larger interval with the same affine parameter. Geodesic completeness means every maximal affine solution has parameter domain all of $\mathbb R$.

items.title: Local Sobolev stability and continuation for the reduced electrovacuum system

references.title: P. T. Chruściel, An introduction to the Cauchy problem for the Einstein equations, Roscoff lecture notes (2011), §1.6, printed pp. 23–25.
M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009), §II.C, printed pp. 8–9.

items.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the conditional local existence theorem [[thm-emg-local-high-sobolev-electrovacuum]]. Let $s\ge5$, let a harmonic-reduced source-free Einstein–Maxwell solution on $[t_0,T)$ have first-order state $U=(g,p,q,e,b)\in L^\infty H^s\cap C H^{s-1}$ with $\partial_tU\in L^\infty H^{s-1}$, and suppose its values stay in a fixed compact admissible state set and $\sup_{t<T}\|U(t)\|_{H^s}<\infty$. If $T$ is finite and lies inside the smooth coefficient-time domain, the reduced solution extends through $T$ to a larger interval. If the original state has $p=\bar\nabla_0g$, $q_i=\bar\nabla_i g$, vanishing harmonic vector $H$, and satisfies the full source-free Einstein–Maxwell equations, the extension has these same properties and extends the full development. The same conclusion holds at a finite left endpoint. On every common interval where two reduced solutions have the same fixed harmonic background, compact-state range and uniform $H^s$ bound, their states are unique and satisfy an $H^{s-1}$ continuous-dependence estimate.

items.title: Smooth local geometric existence and uniqueness for source-free Einstein–Maxwell data

references.title: P. T. Chruściel, An introduction to the Cauchy problem for the Einstein equations, Roscoff lecture notes (2011), §1.6 and the local Cauchy-problem discussion.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric covariant tensor $K$, and smooth spatial vectors $e,b$. Fix $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, use signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, and suppose the four Einstein–Maxwell constraints of [[thm-emg-gauss-codazzi-maxwell-constraints]] hold. In SI convention use length coordinate $x^0=ct$, dimensionless $g,h$, $K$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and $e=E/c$, $b=B$ in tesla. Reconstruct the complete initial two-form on $\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$ by
$$F(N,\mathsf e_i)=-e_i,\qquad F(\mathsf e_i,\mathsf e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k,$$
where $N$ is the future unit normal symbol and $(\mathsf e_i)$ is a positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame. Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local source-free Einstein–Maxwell development on an open variable-width neighborhood of the entire initial surface. After restriction to a smaller collar, the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing, time-orientation-preserving isometry carrying $F$ to $F$. There is no uniform positive time width for noncompact $\Sigma$ and no global-in-time conclusion.

items.title: Causal and Cauchy-surface inputs for smooth electrovacuum developments

references.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations — a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015), Definitions and Theorems 2.6–2.8, printed pp. 10–12, and complete proofs §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 12–24.

items.statement:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold with the causal-curve and global-hyperbolicity conventions of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] and [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. The following interfaces are available for the local and global geometry of smooth electrovacuum developments:

1. Every point has an arbitrarily small strictly convex normal neighborhood. For a future causal curve $\sigma$ in such a neighborhood from $p$, its length satisfies $L_g(\sigma)\le\sqrt{-g_p(v,v)}$, where $v=\exp_p^{-1}(\sigma(1))$. Equality is characterized by the reparametrized radial geodesic when $v$ is future timelike and the curve does not return to $p$ after its start. The future causal and timelike sets are the exponential images of their tangent cones.
2. Each connected component admits a complete auxiliary Riemannian metric. The causal relation is closed, and the causal hull $J^+(K_1)\cap J^-(K_2)$ of two compact sets is compact.
3. Let $h$ be the complete auxiliary metric $h\prime$ of [[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] clause (b), and let $\alpha_k:[0,b_k]\to M$, $0<b_k<\infty$, be future causal curves parametrized by $h$-arclength, with $\alpha_k(0)\to x$ and $\alpha_k(b_k)\to z$ in $M$. After passage to a subsequence with $b_k\to b\in[0,\infty]$, the bounded-length, zero-length and unbounded-length conclusions of [[thm-gr-limit-curve-two-endpoints]] hold: for $0<b<\infty$ the common-domain reparametrizations converge uniformly to a joining causal curve, for $b=0$ the curves converge uniformly on their varying domains to $x=z$, and for $b=\infty$ the forward and backward tails converge on compact parameter intervals to the respective inextendible curves with the supplier's sequential closure relation. Strong causality excludes the unbounded case when all images lie in one compact set.
4. Lorentzian time separation is finite on causal pairs in a globally hyperbolic spacetime, is attained by a causal geodesic, is upper semicontinuous, and is continuous at timelike-related points, with the degenerate coincident-endpoint case as specified in [[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]].
5. Every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface has a variable-width temporal neighborhood whose intrinsic domain-of-dependence interior is globally hyperbolic with that hypersurface Cauchy. Every globally hyperbolic spacetime also admits a smooth Cauchy temporal splitting as in [[thm-gr-smooth-cauchy-temporal-splitting]].

These are mathematical causal inputs. They add no field equations, empirical assumptions, completeness conclusion for causal geodesics, or uniform time-width assertion for noncompact hypersurfaces.

items.title: Source-free smooth maximal globally hyperbolic Einstein–Maxwell development

references.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations — a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015), Definitions and Theorems 2.6–2.8, printed pp. 10–12, and complete proofs §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 12–24.
P. T. Chruściel, An introduction to the Cauchy problem for the Einstein equations, Roscoff lecture notes (2011), complete notes, especially §1.6 and the local Cauchy-problem discussion.

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty connected smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$, and smooth spatial vectors $e,b$. Fix the source-free Einstein–Maxwell model, its constants $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, orientation and $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ convention as in [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. Assume the four constraints of [[thm-emg-gauss-codazzi-maxwell-constraints]] and reconstruct the complete initial two-form by $F(N,\mathsf e_i)=-e_i$, $F(\mathsf e_i,\mathsf e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}b_k$. Then there is a smooth connected time-oriented globally hyperbolic development $(M_{\max},g_{\max},F_{\max},\iota)$ into which every other smooth source-free Einstein–Maxwell development of these complete data embeds by a time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding fixing $\iota$ and carrying $F$ to $F_{\max}$. The maximal development is unique up to a unique such data-fixing isometry. This maximality is within the smooth globally hyperbolic development class for this fixed two-form model; it asserts no geodesic completeness, no maximality among rough or non-globally-hyperbolic extensions, and no global-in-time regularity estimate. Here an affinely parametrized metric geodesic solves $\ddot x^a+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\dot x^b\dot x^c=0$ on an interval; maximality of that solution forbids extension to a strictly larger interval with the same affine parameter. Geodesic completeness means every maximal affine geodesic has parameter domain all of $\mathbb R$.

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009), §II, printed pp. 3–8.

items.statement:
Fix $L_0>0$ and dimensionless periodic coordinates $\theta^i\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, with length coordinates $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ as in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. Let $h=\sum_i dX^i\otimes dX^i=L_0^2\sum_i d\theta^i\otimes d\theta^i$ on the flat periodic torus $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ (thus $h_{ij}=\delta_{ij}$ in the length-coordinate frame), take $\Lambda=0$, and choose two nonzero vectors with constant components $e,b\in\mathbb R^3$ in its oriented orthonormal frame $\partial_{X^i}$ parallel to one another. In the SI convention $e=E/c$ and $b=B$, set
$$H:=\sqrt{\frac{\kappa}{6\mu_0}\bigl(|e|^2+|b|^2\bigr)},\qquad K_{ij}:=Hh_{ij},$$
where $x^0=ct$ is a length coordinate. Then $(h,K,e,b)$ satisfies the source-free Einstein–Maxwell Hamiltonian, momentum and Gauss constraints with $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$. Consequently, conditional on the local theorem's stated CP01 suppliers, these data have a nontrivial smooth source-free local Einstein–Maxwell development.

items.title: Maximality of the Einstein–Maxwell GHD does not assert geodesic completeness

references.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations — a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015), Definitions and Theorems 2.6–2.8, printed pp. 10–12, and complete proofs §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 12–24.
M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009), §II.C, printed pp. 8–9.

items.statement: For the maximal smooth globally hyperbolic development in [[thm-emg-sourcefree-smooth-maximal-development]], maximality means that every development of the same complete source-free data admits a data-fixing development embedding into it, in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]. By [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], an affinely parametrized geodesic for its metric-selected connection is a smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ satisfying $D_\lambda\dot\gamma=0$; in coordinates $y^\mu$ this is $\ddot y^\mu+\Gamma^\mu{}_{\alpha\beta}(y)\dot y^\alpha\dot y^\beta=0$. That theorem supplies a unique maximal solution $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ through each initial datum $(p,v)$, with $I_{p,v}$ an open interval; here **inextendible** means that the curve is such a maximal solution, so no geodesic on a strictly larger interval with the same affine parameter restricts to it. Geodesic completeness means that every such maximal geodesic has parameter domain all of $\mathbb R$. The maximality conclusion by itself asserts no geodesic-completeness property. This remark does not claim that a particular Einstein–Maxwell maximal development is geodesically incomplete.
